objective_for_doctor: A 53-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have swollen or painful lymph nodes, sensitive pain, and burning pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having swollen and painful lymph nodes, and the pain feels sensitive and burning. Also I’ve had some episodes where I lose consciousness or have seizures, and I’m pretty short of breath; my eyes are also red.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent. To understand what’s causing your swollen, burning lymph-node pain and your episodes of fainting/seizures with shortness of breath and red eyes, I need to ask a few quick questions: **(1)** How long has this been going on, and did it start suddenly or gradually?  
Doctor: **(2)** Do you have fever or chills, recent infections (skin sores/leg wound/STD), or any unintentional weight loss?

It started fairly fast—about 4/10 on the speed scale—and I can’t say it’s been long, but it feels like it came on relatively quickly. I don’t have fever or chills that I know of, and I haven’t noticed any recent infections, wounds, or weight loss.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—next questions: **(3)** Where are the swollen nodes (neck, armpit, groin), and do they feel soft/mobile or hard/fixed? **(4)** When you “lose consciousness,” do you have a prodrome (lightheadedness, sweating, palpitations) and do you bite your tongue or have injuries afterward?

The swollen/painful nodes feel like they’re in the neck area. They’re tender and sensitive, but I’m not sure if they’re soft or hard, and I don’t know about “fixed” versus “mobile.” For the losing consciousness, I don’t remember a clear warning like sweating or palpitations, and I haven’t noticed tongue biting or injuries afterward.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—question **(5)**: Have you had any recent mouth/throat pain, dental issues, ear pain, or a new cough/sore throat; and **(6)** any genital sores/discharge or rash?  
Doctor: Also, I need **(7)**: when was the last seizure/fainting episode, and did anyone observe convulsions or just a sudden collapse?  
Doctor: Finally **(8)**: are you having chest pain, sweating with breathlessness, or coughing blood, and are your red eyes painful with light sensitivity or just redness?

I haven’t had mouth or throat pain, dental problems, ear pain, or a new cough or sore throat. I also don’t have genital sores or discharge or any rash.

The last episode of losing consciousness was recently, but I can’t give an exact date/time. I’m not sure if anyone saw convulsions versus just sudden collapse. I don’t have chest pain or coughing blood, and I’m not sure about sweating with breathlessness. My eyes are red, and I don’t know if they’re painful with light sensitivity—more just redness.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—quickly: **(9)** do you currently have vision changes or eye pain (especially with bright light), and **(10)** any swollen nodes elsewhere (armpits/groin) or a skin rash you haven’t mentioned?  
Doctor: **(11)** During those collapse episodes, were you confused afterward (post-episode confusion), and **(12)** do you have severe headaches or new focal neurologic symptoms (weakness, speech trouble)?

Right now I don’t notice vision changes, and I don’t have eye pain that’s worse with bright light—just red eyes.

I don’t have swollen nodes elsewhere like armpits or groin, and I don’t have any rash beyond what I already mentioned. After the collapse I’m not sure about confusion, and I don’t have severe headaches or new weakness or speech trouble that I’ve noticed.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—question **(13)**: have you had unintentional weight loss or drenching night sweats, and **(14)** any painful swallowing, hoarseness, or a persistent throat/neck mass?  
Doctor: Also **(15)**: do you have a history of immunosuppression (HIV, transplant, steroids), smoking, or heavy alcohol use?  
Doctor: Finally **(16)**: any recent tick bites, travel, or contact with TB/anyone with chronic cough?

I haven’t had unintentional weight loss or drenching night sweats. I don’t have painful swallowing, hoarseness, or a persistent throat/neck mass that I can tell.

I don’t know about immunosuppression—I’m not on transplant meds or long-term steroids, and I don’t have a known HIV diagnosis. I don’t smoke and I don’t drink heavily. I haven’t had tick bites, and my recent travel hasn’t been international, and I don’t know of any TB contact.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—question **(17)**: do the red eyes come with sticky discharge or a gritty/burning feeling, and have you noticed a painful eye lump or blurred vision? **(18)**: any recent headaches/neck stiffness, and do the swollen nodes hurt more when you swallow?  
Doctor: Also **(19)**: can you describe the breathlessness—is it worse lying flat or with exertion, and do you have any leg swelling or one-sided calf pain?

My red eyes sometimes feel kind of burning, but I don’t know about sticky discharge or gritty feeling. I haven’t noticed a painful lump in the eye, and I’m not sure about blurred vision.

I don’t have a new headache or neck stiffness. The swollen nodes are tender generally, and I think they might hurt more when I swallow, but I’m not 100% sure.

For breathlessness, it’s worse with exertion and I don’t know about worse when lying flat. I don’t have leg swelling or one-sided calf pain.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—two last key questions: **(20)** have you had any sore throat/“flu-like” illness in the last 1–3 weeks or recent exposure to strep/mono, and are you vaccinated/any risk for meningitis? Also, I need you checked now for emergency causes: are you currently having chest pain, severe shortness of breath, high fever, or confusion?

I haven’t had a sore throat or flu-like illness in the last 1–3 weeks, and I don’t know of any exposure to strep or mono. I don’t know my meningitis vaccine status.

Right now I’m not having chest pain, and I’m not confused. I don’t know if I have a high fever, but I don’t feel severely ill right now beyond the shortness of breath and the lymph node pain.

Doctor: Given your **tender neck lymph nodes plus burning/red eyes** with **recent episodes of collapse/seizures and exertional shortness of breath**, I’m concerned about a serious inflammatory/infectious process involving the eyes/neck and possibly the CNS or lungs—this can’t be safely narrowed without urgent data.  
REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff  
REQUEST TEST: CMP  
REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP  
REQUEST TEST: HIV_test (4th_gen)  
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray  
REQUEST TEST: CT_Head_without_contrast  
REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_puncture_with_CSF_analysis (cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain/culture, viral PCR, AFB if indicated)  
REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmology_urgent_eval (slit-lamp; check for uveitis/conjunctivitis)  
REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_with_contrast OR Ultrasound_Neck_Lymph_nodes (whichever is fastest/available)

Yes, doctor—please do all those tests. I’m worried this could be serious, especially with my shortness of breath and the collapse episodes, so I agree with the CBC, CMP, ESR/CRP, HIV test, chest imaging, CT head, and the eye exam.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—thank you; since you’ve had collapse/seizure-like episodes with exertional shortness of breath plus tender neck nodes and burning/red eyes, this could be life-threatening or neurologic/ocular/infectious, so I want you treated as urgent now.  
Doctor: While we await results from **CBC, CMP, ESR/CRP, HIV (4th gen), Chest X-ray, CT head, lumbar puncture/CSF studies, urgent ophthalmology slit-lamp exam, and CT neck/US nodes**, I need you to go to the ER immediately for monitoring (oxygen/telemetry) and to prevent missed meningitis/encephalitis, disseminated infection, or other emergency causes.
Okay, doctor. I understand this is urgent and I’ll go to the ER right now for monitoring and the tests you ordered.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while you’re heading to the ER, please tell them this exact combination: **tender neck lymph nodes with burning/red eyes** plus **recent collapse/seizure-like episodes** and **exertional shortness of breath** (no fever/chills you’ve noticed, no sore throat/dental/STD symptoms).  
Doctor: I also want them to treat first-pass safety: **continuous pulse-ox/telemetry, IV access, urgent neuro + eye evaluation, and consider empiric antibiotics/antivirals only after cultures/LP are obtained** if they suspect CNS infection.

Yes—doctor. I’ll tell the ER the exact combination: tender neck lymph nodes with burning/red eyes, recent collapse/seizure-like episodes, and exertional shortness of breath. I’ll also mention no fever/chills I’ve noticed and no sore throat/dental/STD symptoms, and I’ll ask them to do continuous pulse-ox/telemetry, IV access, urgent neuro and eye evaluation, and to consider empiric antibiotics/antivirals only after cultures/LP if they suspect CNS infection.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent. I’m not yet able to make a safe diagnosis because I don’t have any of the test results you consented to, and your combination of seizure-like episodes + exertional shortness of breath + tender neck nodes + red/burning eyes could represent several emergencies (e.g., CNS infection/meningitis-encephalitis, disseminated infection, or another inflammatory process).  
Doctor: Please return once the ER has completed and shared the results of **CBC/CMP/ESR-CRP, HIV 4th gen, chest X-ray, CT head, CT neck or node ultrasound, and the urgent eye exam/LP if done**—then I’ll give you a diagnosis.

Okay, doctor—I understand. I’ll stay in the ER and once they’ve done and shared the CBC/CMP/ESR-CRP, HIV test, chest X-ray, CT head, CT neck or ultrasound, and the urgent eye exam (and LP if they do it), I’ll come back to you with the results.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since you’re still waiting on the ER workup, I can’t diagnose yet; please tell me the exact results and any final ER impression.  
Doctor: In particular, I need: CBC (WBC), ESR/CRP, HIV result, chest X-ray/CT findings, CT head/neck findings, and eye exam/LP CSF results (cell count, protein, glucose, culture/PCR).  
Doctor: Once you bring those back, I’ll provide a diagnosis.

If you want, I can tell you what the ER staff say their “working impression” is once they update me.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since you don’t have the test results yet, I need 3 quick specifics to steer the working diagnosis: (1) did the ER perform a lumbar puncture and what were CSF WBC/protein/glucose? (2) did CT head show any focal lesion/meningitis signs? (3) did your eye exam diagnose conjunctivitis vs uveitis/keratitis?  
Doctor: If you can’t answer those yet, at least tell me your most recent oxygen saturation/heart rate and whether they started any IV antibiotics/antivirals already.

I don’t have those details yet—I'm not the one reviewing the CSF numbers or the CT/eye exam findings, and I don’t know whether they did the lumbar puncture or what the results were.

While you’re in the ER, please ask the team for the exact **CSF opening pressure + WBC/protein/glucose**, **CT head/neck reads**, and **eye slit-lamp impression**; then bring them back and I’ll finalize the diagnosis.

Okay, doctor. I’ll ask the ER team for the exact CSF opening pressure and CSF WBC/protein/glucose, the CT head/neck radiology reads, and the eye slit-lamp impression, and I’ll bring those back to you as soon as I get them.
